properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued July 28 at 3:16PM MDT until July 28 at 3:45PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 316 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 5 miles south of
North Sterling Reservoir, or 7 miles northwest of Sterling, moving
east at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Ping pong ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail
damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect wind
damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Sterling, Iliff, North Sterling Reservoir, Padroni and Logan
Corners.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 28 at 3:09PM MDT until July 28 at 6:15PM MDT by NWS Denver CO

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 28 at 1:55PM MDT until July 28 at 4:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:

expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the warning area
will cause debris flows near steep terrain. A debris flow can consist
of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms in and around the
Buckhorn Creek Basin within the Cameron Peak Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flooding of areas in and around the Buckhorn Creek Basin
within the Cameron Peak Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of East Central Larimer County.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Redstone Creek, Eld Creek, North Fork Fish Creek, Buckhorn Creek,
Pennock Creek, Sheep Creek and Cedar Creek.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 28 at 12:13PM MDT until July 28 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive
rainfall over the Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar are possible.

* WHERE...Gold Mountain Fire Burn Scar in Ouray County Colorado,
including Dexter Creek and Cutler Creek, particularly along
highway 550, and Cow Creek.

* WHEN...Until 800 PM MDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Excessive rainfall is possible over the Gold Mountain
Burn Scar which could lead to flash flooding and/or debris flows,
particularly along highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter
Creek. Cow creek may also be affected. The debris flow can consist
of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1202 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Gold Mountain Burn Scar, including Cow Creek, and along
highway 550 between Cutler Creek and Dexter Creek.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
